findings.issue: The slot `distributions` does not exist in the supplied schema digest. The digest's Dataset/CoreDataset slot inventory declares `distribution_formats` (range DistributionFormat) and `file_collections` (range FileCollection); no slot named `distributions` is listed, and no object range in the digest declares the keys used here (`path`, `format`, `media_type`, `md5`, `bytes`). The full record correctly used `file_collections` with FileCollection objects. This block will almost certainly fail validation against CoreDataset; the per-file content should be carried by `file_collections` (if CoreDataset declares it) or omitted.
Key `md5` is not declared on any object range in the digest. Checksums are declared on DistributionFormat as `checksum`. Even if the containing slot were corrected, `md5` is an invented key (#380).

`conforms_to_standard` is applied to a per-file object (cm4ai_release_metadata.zip) whose class is not declared in the digest; only Dataset, DataSubset and FileCollection are shown as accepting that slot. Compounds the invented-slot problem above.

`resources` has range Dataset (per the digest), whose only required key is `id`, and which accepts the full Dataset slot inventory. The two arm objects use `keywords`, `name`, `description`, `id` — all valid — but the full record modelled these same two arms as `subsets` (range DataSubset), where the semantically load-bearing flags `is_data_split: false` and `is_subpopulation: false` were populated. Projecting them into `resources` silently drops that discrimination without a source_caveat explaining the change. If CoreDataset declares `subsets`, that is the correct target.

counts: 53788 is attached to an Instance object describing MDA-MB-468 immunofluorescence images in this release, but the accompanying source_caveats states the figure is the project-wide portal total across all releases and both cell lines. A count that does not count the instances of the object it sits on is a mis-scoped value; the caveat mitigates but does not repair it. Preferable to omit `counts` and retain the portal figure in `notes`.
Same mis-scoped count carried forward from the full record with the same caveat. Same disposition applies.

The bundle's Dataverse citation lists 47 named authors with affiliations and ORCIDs for the June 2026 release. Only seven are represented as Creator objects. The digest declares `creators` multivalued, and the bundle plainly supports one object per distinct author. Selecting seven leads is defensible only if stated; the source_caveats note (#11) explains the credit_roles provenance but does not state or justify the truncation of the author list itself.

`affiliations` (range Organization[]) is unpopulated on every Creator, while institutional affiliation is stated in prose inside `notes` (e.g. 'The Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco...', 'lead for the Standards module at the University of Virginia'). The bundle gives an institution name for every author. Populating a declared structured field via free text is the defect the v3 rule names; Organization requires only `id`, so name-only Organization objects were available.

The single InformedConsent object populates only `notes` and `source_caveats`; every declared field (`consent_obtained`, `consent_type`, `consent_scope`, `consent_documentation`, `withdrawal_mechanism`) is empty, and the source_caveats explicitly states no field could be populated from evidence. An object of the correct shape carrying none of the structure it exists to hold is not an answer; the slot should be omitted and the ethical-sourcing statement retained in the full record's `collection_consents` equivalent or in `notes`.

Omitted from the core record while `informed_consent` was populated in its place. The full record used `collection_consents` for exactly this content. If CoreDataset declares `collection_consents`, the projection has moved evidence into a neighbouring slot that asks a different question (procedural consent record vs. consent obtained for collection) without noting the substitution.

`committee_name: Data Access Committee` is paired with `committee_contact: Jillian Parker`, but the record's own source_caveats (#governance) states the bundle names two possibly distinct bodies — a 'Data Access Committee' (preprint) and a 'Data Governance Committee' with Parker as contact (Dataverse metadata) — and that the sources do not state whether they are the same. Asserting the preprint's committee name alongside the Dataverse metadata's contact merges two entities the evidence keeps separate. The caveat discloses the conflict but the slot value still resolves it.
Same merge of two possibly distinct committees, carried forward with the same caveat.

Person object uses `id: https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4535-3486` for Jillian Parker. That ORCID appears in the bundle's author lists for 'Parker J'; the governance contact is given in the release metadata only as a name and email (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu). Equating the two is a reasonable but unstated inference, and the email — the identifier the bundle actually supplies for this role — is carried only in `stewardship_roles` prose.

Two ethical review contacts are named in the bundle (Ravitsky and Bélisle-Pipon); `contact_person` is single-valued so only Ravitsky is structured, with Bélisle-Pipon relegated to `review_details` prose. Not a defect given the declared cardinality, but a second EthicalReview object could have carried the second named reviewer.

`role` on DataCollector is not enum-constrained in the digest (unlike Maintainer.role), so the free-text values 'academic research laboratory', 'consortium data acquisition module', 'depositing and packaging institutions' are permissible. Noted only because the last of these is a plural description of several institutions in one object where the slot is multivalued and the bundle names four production locations distinctly.
Same aggregation of four production-location institutions into a single collector object, carried forward.

Only RO_CRATE is asserted at dataset level, which the bundle supports. However `conforms_to` prose also describes JSON-LD/RDF serialisation, EVI and Schema.org vocabularies and ARK identifiers; none maps to a digest enum value, so omission of further terms is correct. No action required — recorded for completeness of the enum audit.

total_file_count: 10 is supported (ten archives listed on the June 2026 landing page), but `total_size_bytes` is omitted while ten per-file sizes are published. The digest describes both as aggregatable from file_collections; sizes are rounded display values (4.6 GB etc.) so exact byte aggregation is not derivable. Omission is the correct call; noted to confirm it was not an oversight.
Present in the full record, absent from the core record, with no source_caveat noting the drop. If CoreDataset declares the slot, the same evidence supports it.

The full record carries the 47-author Dataverse citation; the core record omits it and states in source_caveats #11 that 'the core schema having no citation slot'. The supplied digest is the Dataset inventory and does not enumerate CoreDataset's slots, so this claim about the core schema is asserted rather than shown. If `citation` is in fact declared on CoreDataset, its omission loses the full author list entirely from the core record.

`download_url` is populated on the full record's DistributionFormat but omitted here, while `access_urls` retains the same Dataverse landing-page URI. Minor asymmetry between the paired records with no stated reason; the digest declares both keys on DistributionFormat.

The fifth InstanceAcquisition describes the inferred cell maps, then states they are not included in this release. Documenting an acquisition method for content the record elsewhere says is absent risks reading as a claim about released data. The `was_inferred_derived: true` flag plus the explicit exclusion sentence make the intent legible, so this is borderline rather than a defect.

`id` is the June 2026 release DOI while `name` is the programme-level 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI)'. The description resolves the referent explicitly to the June 2026 release, and both records hold to that choice consistently. Referent selection is documented and coherent.

Substrate terms checked against B2AI_SUBSTRATE: 19=Image, 59=Size Exclusion Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Data, 58=Mass Spectrometry Data, 64=Perturb-seq Data. All four are apt and none is an approximation. Topic terms 19=Microscale Imaging, 28=Proteome, 26=Protein, 34=Transcriptome likewise fit.

All enum values used (representation_bias, selection_bias; scope_limitation, coverage_limitation, temporal_limitation, methodological_limitation) are defined in the digest. No undefined enum members detected across bias_type, limitation_type, relationship_type, credit_roles, collection_type, compression, data_use_permission, confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant, or maintainer role.

Fourteen (full) / fifteen (core) numbered caveats are confined to `source_caveats` at record and object level rather than leaking into names, identifiers or affiliation values. The U2OS/Nature boundary (caveat 1), the release-date conflict (2), the file-date anomaly (3), the protein-count divergence (4) and the project-end-date conflict (5) are each disclosed rather than silently resolved. This is correct handling of the evidence boundary.

summary: Both records are well grounded in the declared bundle, with conflicts disclosed rather than resolved silently and the U2OS/Nature material correctly excluded as a distinct dataset. Enum usage, B2AI substrate and topic terms, and the confinement of source commentary to source_caveats are all clean. The dominant defect is structural and confined to the core record: a `distributions` block that the supplied schema digest does not declare, carrying undeclared keys (`path`, `md5`, `bytes`), where `file_collections` was used correctly in the full record — this is very likely to fail CoreDataset validation and should be corrected before the paired records are considered complete. Two further projection defects accompany it: the two cell-line arms move from `subsets` (DataSubset, with is_data_split/is_subpopulation populated) to `resources` (Dataset) without a stated reason, and `collection_consents` is replaced by an `informed_consent` object whose every declared field is empty by the record's own admission and which should simply be omitted. Across both records, `creators` under-represents a 47-author list without stating the truncation, and no Creator populates the declared `affiliations` field despite the bundle naming an institution for every author, leaving that structure in prose. Two smaller merges warrant attention: the Data Access Committee / Data Governance Committee naming, where a disclosed conflict is nonetheless resolved in the slot value, and an instance `counts` of 53,788 that is a project-wide total attached to a release-scoped object. None of these introduces unsupported factual content; they are shape and fidelity issues rather than provenance breaches.
